data.description:
## Observation
At 2026-10-27 ~18:52 PDT, `git fetch origin` in the shared checkout `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar` failed:

```
fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository
```

`git remote -v` returned **empty** — from the main checkout and from every linked worktree, since they share one config. Inspection:

- `.git/config` was 403 bytes with **no `[remote "origin"]` and no `[remote "gerrit"]` section**.
- `.git/refs/remotes/` did not exist.
- `.git/logs/refs/remotes/` existed but was **empty** — the remote-tracking reflogs were gone too.
- `grep -c refs/remotes .git/packed-refs` returned `0`.
- `.git/config` mtime was **Oct 27 17:36**, inside this session's window.

What SURVIVED in `.git/config`: `[core]`, `[gc] autoDetach = false`, `[maintenance] autoDetach = false`, `[merge "ours"] driver = true`, `[user]` (the bot identity), and a `[credential "https://github.com"]` helper. So the file was not truncated or emptied — it was rewritten minus the two remote sections while rebar's own ADR-0051 gc/maintenance settings and the identity survived.

## Impact
This blocks ALL code work in the repository, and does so at the two points an agent reaches first:

- `make worktree name=<x>` and any `git worktree add … origin/main` fail — no `origin` to branch from. This is the documented entry point for every change in `AGENTS.md`.
- `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main` cannot run — no `gerrit`. Nothing can be sent for review.

It is also silent until used: nothing warns that the remotes went away, and the failure message ("'origin' does not appear to be a git repository") reads like a network or permissions problem rather than a missing config section, which sends an investigator down the wrong path.

## Not established — the cause
I did not modify `.git/config`, and nothing in this session's command history writes to it. Earlier in the same session, pushes to `gerrit` succeeded repeatedly (Gerrit changes 3119, 3120, 3121, 3122, 3123, the last merging at ~14:50 PDT), so both remotes existed and worked for hours before 17:36.

Candidate causes, none confirmed:
1. A concurrent agent session or operator action on this shared host rewrote the config. The repo is explicitly shared — `AGENTS.md` warns the main checkout holds operator WIP and that linked worktrees share one repo-global config.
2. A tool that rewrites `.git/config` wholesale (some credential-helper or identity-management steps do) dropped sections it did not model.
3. Related to a separate fault seen minutes earlier at ~18:40: a local `rebar edit` failed with `git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 30s`, suggesting git operations on this host were already degraded. That write did NOT land (the ticket was unchanged), and the same edit succeeded through the MCP server.

Hypotheses 1 and 2 are untested; 3 is correlation in time only.

## Recovery applied (verified, not guessed)
```sh
git remote add origin https://github.com/navapbc/rebar.git
git remote add gerrit https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/a/rebar
```

The URLs were NOT recalled blind. `gerrit` is the host printed verbatim by this session's own push output (`To https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/a/rebar`). `origin` was then proven by fetching and checking that a commit this session pushed and merged is present and is the branch tip:

```
git fetch origin && git log --oneline -1 origin/main
ee5253abfd4 Document the eval harnesses for client projects
```

A wrong URL would have failed the fetch or lacked that object, so this is empirical confirmation rather than assumption.

## Proposed work
1. Determine the writer. Check shell history, any config-rewriting tooling, and whether a sibling agent session was active at 17:36. Until that is known, the recovery above is a repair, not a fix — it can recur at any moment, including mid-push.
2. Decide whether the remotes should be recorded somewhere recoverable. Today the only record was the config that was lost; a `git remote -v` snapshot in the repo (or a documented restore step in `docs/local-dev-env.md`) turns a blocking mystery into a one-line fix.
3. Consider a preflight in `make worktree`: when `origin` is absent, fail with "the repository has no `origin` remote — see <runbook>" rather than letting raw git emit a message that implies a network fault.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The writer of the 17:36 `.git/config` rewrite is identified, or the investigation records exactly which sources were checked and found silent.
- [ ] The canonical `origin` and `gerrit` URLs are recorded in a tracked file or runbook, so recovery does not depend on scrollback.
- [ ] `make worktree` fails with a message naming the missing remote and pointing at the restore step, instead of surfacing raw git's "does not appear to be a git repository".
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.
data.title: Both git remotes (origin and gerrit) vanished from the shared checkout's .git/config mid-session, blocking all worktree creation and every Gerrit push
